children: The Bank of Ghana left its benchmark interest rate steady at 14.0% during its September 2026 meeting, marking a third consecutive pause, amid inflation risks.
The Committee said the risks to inflation and growth were broadly balanced, while the current policy stance was aimed at bringing inflation toward the central bank’s medium-term target of 8%.
Meanwhile, Governor Johnson Asiama highlighted renewed economic risks from the escalating Middle East crisis, warning that higher energy and fertiliser costs could add to inflationary pressures.
Ghana’s headline inflation quickened to 5.0% in August from 4.6% in July.

title: Bank of Ghana Holds Rate for Third Meeting
